description: Screenshot of an anonymous imageboard post dated 01/23/18 with two attached image excerpts, presented against a black background (mobile screenshot letterboxing). The first attachment is a cropped Q-post excerpt asking why seven people traveled to a secured undisclosed meeting after the election and why HRC gave no concession speech. The second is a cropped news-article excerpt in which Trey Gowdy, speaking to Martha MacCallum, describes a text exchange between two FBI agents mentioning an insurance policy and a first meeting of the secret society. The poster comments that a Q question was finally partially answered.
text: Anonymous 01/23/18 (Tue) 08:20:24 ID: d96cd9 No.135162 >>135169 >>135173. File (hide): 2810b8b5216b3c1….png (32.93 KB, 413x102, 413:102, Screen Shot 2018-01-23 at ….png) (h) (u). Perhaps he could not in good conscious see the world burn. Why, hours after the election, did seven people travel to an undisclosed location to hold a very private & highly secured/guarded meeting? Why didn't HRC give a concession speech? When was the last time a presidential candidate didn't. File (hide): 1551b5c467fbaff….png (72.16 KB, 673x216, 673:216, Screen Shot 2018-01-23 at ….png) (h) (u). McCallum's interest was piqued. She asked Gowdy for additional details. "You have this insurance policy in the Spring of 2016 and then the day after the election  … there's a text exchange between these two FBI agents -- these two (supposed to be objective, fact-centric) FBI agents saying, 'perhaps this is the first meeting of the secret society,'" Gowdy explained. "So of course I'm gonna want to know what 'secret society' are you talking about -- because you're supposed to be investigating objectively the person who just won the Electoral College."
flags: Q-post questions and the secret society characterization are the posts' claims, not established facts
the two FBI agents are not named in the image (widely reported as Strzok and Page) - not asserted here

description: Screenshot of the Signal encrypted-messenger homepage (Open Whisper Systems era design). Blue header with Signal logo and nav links; tagline 'Fast, simple, secure. Privacy that fits in your pocket.' with Android, iPhone and Desktop download links. A phone mockup shows a demo Signal chat with a contact labeled 'Friedrich Nietzsche, University of Basel' containing a waterfall photo and a Nietzsche quote. A row of endorser portraits is partially cropped at the bottom; the leftmost is Edward Snowden, and others are consistent with Laura Poitras and Bruce Schneier.
text: Signal. SUPPORT. BLOG. DEVELOPERS. JOBS. Fast, simple, secure. Privacy that fits in your pocket. Android. iPhone. Desktop. 6:41. Friedrich Nietzsche. University of Basel. Today. Just now. We should consider every day lost on which we have not danced at least once. And we should call every truth false which was not accompanied by at least one laugh. Just now. Signal message.
flags: cropped endorser portraits besides Snowden are consistent with Laura Poitras and Bruce Schneier but not certain (faces partially cut off, no captions visible)
